extracted.intended_audience: AI/ML researchers building or evaluating LLMs on advanced mathematical reasoning; benchmark designers
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating an Olympiad-level mathematical-reasoning benchmark (RIMO) for LLMs, with two tracks: numeric-answer problems (RIMO-N) and proof problems (RIMO-P). The benchmark emphasizes deterministic, high-resolution evaluation while preserving Olympiad difficulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve Olympiad-level difficulty while eliminating evaluation noise
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve peak Olympiad difficulty while eliminating this evaluation noise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design should keep the original challenge of IMO problems but remove sources of grading noise and bias that plague existing benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single, unique integer answer for numeric track (RIMO-N)
rubrics_metrics.description: RIMO-N rewrites 335 IMO problems to admit a single, unique integer answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problems that admit one integer answer enable deterministic correctness checking and avoid heterogeneous answer-format issues and model-based judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deterministic correctness checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow deterministic correctness checking by using answer formats (e.g., single integer) that can be checked without model-based judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deterministic checks reduce grading noise and bias compared to free-form or heterogeneous answer formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof-track with expert-checked solutions (RIMO-P)
rubrics_metrics.description: RIMO-P features 456 proof problems with expert-checked solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert verification of solutions is used to ensure ground-truth correctness and to avoid reliance on potentially flawed solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decompose proofs into a sequence of sub-problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof problems are decomposed into a sequence of sub-problems to evaluate the step-by-step reasoning process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decomposition permits fine-grained assessment of intermediate reasoning steps rather than only final answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated grading of step-by-step reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the step-by-step reasoning process via an automated grading system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automation over sub-problem checks enables scalable, repeatable grading of proofs and intermediate steps while reducing human grading burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate heterogeneous answer formats and model-based judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid heterogeneous answer formats that require model-based judges, which introduce grading noise and potential bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer uniform, machine-checkable answer formats (e.g., unique integers) or structured sub-problem checks to minimize reliance on subjective/model judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reliance on potentially flawed solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on potentially flawed solutions as ground truth; instead use expert-checked solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert checking increases trustworthiness of benchmark solutions and reduces evaluation errors caused by incorrect reference solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-track benchmark structure (RIMO-N and RIMO-P)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide two complementary tracks: numeric-answer problems (RIMO-N) and proof problems with stepwise evaluation (RIMO-P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A two-track design balances easy-to-evaluate formats with rich proof-oriented evaluation to measure both final-answer correctness and stepwise reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-resolution, challenging yet easy-to-evaluate suite
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a challenging yet easy-to-evaluate suite that yields a high-resolution yardstick for future research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark should distinguish current LLM capabilities from true Olympiad-level reasoning, exposing gaps that older benchmarks obscure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical benchmarking against frontier LLMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmark should be used to evaluate frontier LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Flash) to reveal their performance on the suite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons to older benchmarks help demonstrate that high scores on prior datasets do not imply competence on RIMO; use multiple models to characterize the gap.
